headline: No plausible pairwise harm pathway: both agents are non-runnable, offline, and expose no shared write or data surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero and spring-integration-samples expose no shared communication channel, no MCP, no filesystem access, and no browser or subprocess surfaces. With both profiles marked runnable:false and network_egress:none, there is no plausible default injection bridge between them.
conditions: IF either agent is later wrapped with a shared clipboard, queue, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF either profile gains file-reading or instruction-parsing from external content, the pathway may open.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or message bus.
Do not add an MCP server or shared workspace without provenance tracking.
Reassess if either agent becomes runnable or gains browser/file ingestion.
requires-engineering: add explicit content provenance labels at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile touches data classes, and both report network_egress:none. LightZero has no filesystem read/write, while spring-integration-samples exposes no data surfaces. There is no documented path for one agent to leak the other's data in the current configuration.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk changes.
IF either agent is granted outbound network access, reassess exfiltration risk.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Leave outbound network disabled for both agents.
Verify no OAuth or API credentials are mounted into either runtime.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation and secret-scanning controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses; spring-integration-samples only documents network_egress:none. With no overlapping mutable resource access, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk may emerge.
IF either agent is later given git or database mutation rights, reassess coordination needs.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current deployment.
Avoid mounting a shared writable repo or database.
If writes are added, serialize access with an external lock.
requires-engineering: implement resource-level locking for any future shared mutable target.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The pair has no action-taking authority and no documented input/output bridge. LightZero is a game-playing repo, while spring-integration-samples is a travel-planning sample repo; neither profile shows that B consumes A's outputs as authoritative or acts on them.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding LightZero outputs directly into spring-integration-samples workflows, reassess.
IF either agent is given downstream execution rights, cascading error risk may appear.
mitigations: Do not chain outputs from one agent into the other without verification.
Keep both agents non-runnable in production contexts.
Add a human review step before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between producer and consumer agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched, no residency-sensitive surfaces are documented, and both profiles are open-source docs-only entries. The compliance mismatch pathways in the rubric are not triggered by the current pair.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance.
IF deployment introduces retention or residency requirements, verify them against the runtime.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any future retention or residency policy before deployment.
Review compliance again if either agent becomes a hosted service.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classification and residency.
